commit.message:
Fix critical wire-format bugs found by frontend code-review + live verification

Code-review found the most severe bug in this whole build: wagmi's
signTypedData returns a hex string, but Go's json.Unmarshal into a plain
Signature []byte field (signedEnvelope[T], rfq.go) decodes base64 by
default, not hex. Sent unconverted, a valid signature would silently
base64-decode into 99 garbage bytes and fail recoverSigner's explicit
65-byte length check -- breaking every single OPEN and QUOTE submission.
The project's own Go-to-Go integration test never exposed this because both
sides there used Go's default []byte marshaling consistently; the frontend
uses a different representation and nothing caught the mismatch until this
review. Fixed with an explicit hex-to-base64 conversion before the signature
is placed in the JSON envelope, and verified live against the real TEE
(scripts/verify-signature-encoding.mts) -- a 65-byte dummy signature now
correctly reaches Go's ecrecover step instead of failing the length check.

While building that verification script, found a second, distinct bug the
review didn't catch: bigint fields (size, limitPrice, rfqNonce, expiry) were
JSON-stringified as quoted strings ("1000000"), but Go's
math/big.Int.UnmarshalJSON requires a bare unquoted number and rejects a
string outright ("cannot unmarshal \"1000000\" into a *big.Int").
Fixed with a sentinel-marker + regex-strip approach that preserves full
precision for WAD-scale values exceeding Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, and
verified live the same way.

Also fixed three smaller review findings: the TEE pubkey's x/y coordinates
weren't zero-padded to 32 bytes each before being written into the
65-byte uncompressed key (silently misaligns the byte layout for any
coordinate with a leading zero byte, roughly 1-in-256 odds -- fixed by
reusing the existing padTo32 helper); scripts/verify-ecies.mjs duplicated
the entire ECIES stack by hand instead of importing lib/ecies.ts, meaning a
future fix to the real module wouldn't be caught by re-running
'verification' -- replaced with verify-ecies.mts, which imports the actual
production module via tsx; and ConnectWallet's connect() call had no error
handling, silently swallowing a declined connection with no user feedback.

Production build passes cleanly. Both wire-format fixes are now verified
against the live TEE, not just reasoned about.

Add frontend: taker + maker screens, browser-safe ECIES verified against the live TEE

Scaffolded Next.js app (App Router, wagmi/viem for wallet + Coston2 chain
config) with the two screens from BUILD-SPEC.md §2.3.

The highest-risk new piece was lib/ecies.ts: the frontend needs to encrypt
RFQ payloads to the TEE's pubkey using the exact same scheme go-ethereum's
crypto/ecies package decrypts with (NIST concat-KDF, AES-128-CTR, HMAC-SHA256
tag, specific byte layout) — not a generic ECIES library, which would produce
incompatible ciphertext. De-risked before writing any UI: first proved the
algorithm out in Node (crypto.createECDH), then rewrote it browser-safe (Web
Crypto API + @noble/curves, since Web Crypto's ECDH doesn't support
secp256k1) and re-verified that exact browser-safe version against the live
running TEE via scripts/verify-ecies.mjs. Both passed — decryption succeeded,
failing only at field validation on a deliberately incomplete probe payload.

Taker screen: connect wallet, sign an EIP-712 RfqIntent, approve per the
role-specific rule from BUILD-SPEC.md §2.1 (buy: quoteAmount at the taker's
own limit; sell: exact size — never max uint), open the RFQ via the /direct
client (lib/rfqClient.ts), close it, and watch the Filled event on-chain
rather than trust the close response (which is intentionally async-settled,
see rfq.go's changelog entry).

Maker screen: same signing/approve pattern for Quote, with RFQ id/side/size
entered manually — there is no public RFQ listing, disclosed as an MVP
limitation matching BUILD-SPEC.md §5, not an oversight.

Verified so far: full  passes cleanly, all four routes render
with zero console errors, wallet-connect doesn't crash without an extension
present. Not yet verified: the full approve/sign/submit/settle click-through,
which needs a real wallet with a funded Coston2 account — that's the
remaining funded demo run, a separate step.

Fix critical security regression from the /direct message-shape fix: block non-RFQ OPTypes

Code-review pass on the post-live-test changes found that fixing processAction's
message-shape bug had an unintended side effect: KEY/UPDATE (and KEY/SIGN) became
fully dispatchable via /direct, which has no authentication at that layer.
Before the fix, KEY/UPDATE via /direct always failed with an empty
OriginalMessage — an accidental protection. Removing that bug removed the
protection with it: anyone reaching the tunnel could GET /info for the TEE's
pubkey, encrypt their own chosen private key, and overwrite the extension's
attested-signer key — the exact key RfqSettlement trusts without on-chain
re-verification per the disclosed trust model.

Fixed by hard-rejecting any OPType other than RFQ on the Direct dispatch path.
KEY management stays on the on-chain InstructionSender path only, where
dispatching it costs real gas and leaves an auditable sender.

Verified live against the running stack (not just unit tests): a crafted
KEY/UPDATE direct-dispatch now returns 403 and the extension-side result
shows status:0 with the exact rejection reason; a crafted RFQ/OPEN still
reaches the intended handler and fails cleanly on bad ciphertext, confirming
no regression to the RFQ path itself.

Also fixed: unrecovered panic in the async settle goroutine (net/http's
built-in recover doesn't cover spawned child goroutines — an unhandled panic
there would have crashed the whole process, not just one RFQ); a fast
synchronous config check before spawning that goroutine, so a misconfigured
deployment fails the request instead of silently claiming matched:true with
no way to ever detect the failure; an HTTP response-body leak in the
integration test's poll loop on non-200 responses; and reworked the test's
key-loading step to respect the new security boundary — KEY/UPDATE is no
longer dispatched through the test's own /direct calls, matching the fix.

Fix processAction message-shape bug and async CLOSE; prove the full RFQ flow live on Coston2

Two real bugs found only by actually running this against the live stack,
neither caught by unit tests or code review since both depend on framework
behavior invisible from the extension's own source:

1. processAction assumed action.Data.Message is always DataFixed-shaped JSON.
   True for on-chain InstructionSender dispatch, false for /direct — direct
   actions arrive as DirectInstruction-shaped JSON ({opType,opCommand,message})
   posted unwrapped (traced to tee-node's internal/processors/direct/default.go).
   Parsing that as DataFixed silently left OriginalMessage empty — no error,
   just a wrong-shaped struct. The 'DO NOT MODIFY' boilerplate needed modifying
   because it was only ever exercised via the on-chain path before.

2. tee-node's action-response cycle has a hardcoded, non-configurable 2-second
   timeout (internal/settings.ProxyTimeout). Synchronously dialing the chain,
   fetching chain ID, and broadcasting settle() inside RFQ/CLOSE's handler
   reliably exceeds it. Fixed by submitting asynchronously and reporting only
   the match in the HTTP response — which is arguably the more correct design
   anyway: a frontend should confirm settlement via the on-chain Filled event,
   not by trusting the extension's synchronous word for it.

Added rfq_integration_test.go: a live test (guarded behind RFQ_INTEGRATION_TEST=1,
hermetic otherwise) that runs the complete flow through the actual running
Docker stack over the real ngrok-tunneled /direct endpoint — KEY/UPDATE,
RFQ/OPEN, two RFQ/QUOTE calls, RFQ/CLOSE — and verifies the correct maker
wins. It passes. The settle tx itself was confirmed reaching the chain and
reverting with the exact expected reason (ERC20: insufficient allowance,
since the test wallets are unfunded throwaway keys) — meaning EIP-712
verification, replay/expiry guards, and the FTSO path all passed on-chain,
and only the disclosed non-binding-fill limitation (already in BUILD-SPEC.md)
was what stopped a full settlement.

Fix 8 findings from Go extension code-review pass

Critical: nil-pointer panic on missing big.Int fields in a malformed/malicious
RFQ payload (validateRfqIntent/validateQuote now reject cleanly instead of
crashing the request goroutine). Real bugs: selectWinner never checked the
taker's own RfqIntent expiry, only each quote's — a late CLOSE could sign and
submit a Fill guaranteed to revert on-chain after already reporting matched:true;
negative Size/LimitPrice/Price hashed by absolute value in Go but ABI-encoded
via two's-complement on-chain, silently breaking the signature for a
maliciously-signed negative field. Both rejected at intake now.

DoS hardening: rfqBook.open and usedNonces were unbounded — added
pruneExpired, with usedNonces keyed to each nonce's originating intent expiry
so it's safe to evict once that intent could never succeed again anyway.

Efficiency + correctness: submitSettle redialed the chain and re-fetched
ChainID on every single RFQ close; replaced with a cached settler
(sync.Once) plus an explicit mutex serializing the nonce-fetch-then-send
step, since two concurrent RFQ_CLOSE calls could otherwise be assigned the
same pending nonce.

Style: removed two banner-style comment blocks per CLAUDE.md's explicit rule
against them.

13/13 tests passing, including 4 new regression tests pinning these exact
findings so they can't come back silently.

Add Go extension RFQ logic: EIP-712 signed intents, winner selection, settle submission

Implements BUILD-SPEC.md §2.2 against the corrected architecture (proxy's
/direct endpoint, not a free-form REST API — see the architecture-correction
changelog entry): RFQ_OPEN/RFQ_QUOTE/RFQ_CLOSE op commands, EIP-712 signature
recovery for RfqIntent and Quote (never trusting client-supplied addresses,
the round-2 critical fix), the six-step winner-selection function, and
on-chain settle() submission via a separate gas-paying hot key.

Highest-value test in the file: TestFillDigest_MatchesLiveContract cross-checks
the Go EIP-712 encoding against the actual deployed contract's hashFill output
on Coston2, not just against itself — if Go and Solidity ever disagreed on
encoding, no signature made in Go would validate on-chain. It passes.

9/9 tests passing: the live-contract cross-check, signature recovery
round-trip (+ a negative case), and five winner-selection scenarios (buy,
sell, tie-break, no-match, expired-quote-excluded).

Fix 6 findings from code-review pass: zero-quoteAmount hole (top finding), Math.mulDiv, FTSO decimal bounds, toleranceBps validation, weak test assertions, duplicated transfer branches

Redeployed to Coston2 at 0xaBf47C48c00DDa806f1d9243c936A8153C7E6FcE (the prior
deployment at 0x6aD574AA... has the zero-quoteAmount hole and should not be used).
Now settling against real USDT0 (0xC1A5...) as quoteToken, not a self-issued mock -
both FXRP and USDT0 addresses confirmed live via the Coston2 explorer API, not a
web search or Telegram screenshot.

9/9 Foundry tests passing, including a new regression test for the zero-amount bug.

Add RfqSettlement contract: signed-intent settlement, EIP-712, live-read decimals, FTSO price bound

- Fixes round-1's decimal-math bug (was off by 10^12) and round-3's FTSO decimal
  normalization bug found while writing the tests, not by inspection
- 8 Foundry tests passing: required buy/sell decimal-math pair, replay guard,
  expiry guard, untrusted-signer guard, FTSO bound (within/outside/stale, mocked)
- isAttestedSigner is an MVP owner-controlled placeholder for the real
  TeeExtensionRegistry check per BUILD-SPEC.md 4.1b - not yet confirmed live
Add fce-sign FCC scaffold, confirm go/no-go on Coston2 (simulated TEE, pre-build + post-build + test all passing)
